Per-group psychometric networks

Source: R/groups.R
psychnet_group.Rd

The object returned by psychnet() when group is supplied: a named list of psychnet networks, one per level of the grouping variable. It plots as a grid with cograph::splot() and is consumed per level by the framework verbs (net_centralities(), net_predict(), net_boot(), net_stability(), net_compare()), each returning a *_group result. Data-based resampling and comparison require independent cross-sectional rows. Groups built from several occasions per actor need resampling at the actor level and are refused by these row-based diagnostics.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A psychnet_group object.

...

Ignored.

row.names, optional

Ignored (S3 consistency).

object

A psychnet_group object.

Value

x, invisibly (for print), after printing one row per group with its node and edge counts and sample size.

For as.data.frame, the per-group edge lists stacked with a leading group column: one row per edge per group, columns group, from, to, weight.

For summary, a data frame with node/edge counts and mean absolute edge weight: one row per group, or per group and level when a group contains within/between networks.

Details

Networks are listed in the grouping variable's level order when it is a factor (so its first level is group 1 of net_compare()), otherwise in order of first appearance. Rows with a missing group value are dropped with a psychnet_rows_dropped warning; an empty-string level, or a cross-sectional level with fewer than 3 rows, is a psychnet_bad_input error; a level with no more rows than variables raises a psychnet_small_sample warning.

Examples

d <- rbind(data.frame(SRL_GPT, source = "GPT"),
           data.frame(SRL_Claude, source = "Claude"))
nets <- psychnet(d, method = "glasso", group = "source")
nets
#> <psychnet_group> 2 networks by source (method: glasso)
#>   group nodes edges   n
#>     GPT     5    10 300
#>  Claude     5    10 300
summary(nets)
#>    group nodes edges mean_abs_weight
#> 1    GPT     5    10       0.2444301
#> 2 Claude     5    10       0.3536997
as.data.frame(nets)
#>     group from to       weight
